#!/usr/bin/env bash
find /usr/local/bin -type f -executable -exec file {} \; | grep -i ELF | cut -d: -f1 | while read -r bin; do
  if [ $(stat -c %U "$bin") != "root" ]; then

  fi
done

logfile=myapp.log
# Rotate
if [ -f "$logdir/$logfile" ]; then
  mv "$logdir/$logfile" "$logdir/${logfile}.$yesterday"
  gzip "$logdir/${logfile}.$yesterday"
fi
# Create new log file with proper perms

# Cleanup old archives

Write a Bash function that monitors a directory (/var/spool/queue) for new files, processes each file by sending its contents via HTTP POST to https://api.example.com/ingest, moves successfully sent files to /var/spool/processed, and retries failed ones up to 3 times with exponential backoff.
command:
process_queue(){
  inotifywait -m -e close_write --format '%w%f' /var/spool/queue | while read -r file; do
    attempts=0
    while ((attempts<3)); do
      if curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' --data-binary "@$file" https://api.example.com/ingest; then
        mv "$file" /var/spool/processed/
        break
      else
        ((attempts++))
        sleep $((2**attempts))
      fi
    done
    if ((attempts==3)); then
      mv "$file" /var/spool/failed/
    fi
  done
}
